issue_context.title: pandas.read_pickle can take buffer object as well, not only str
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/62a87bf4a2af02a8d3bc271ad26e5994292b8e6a/pandas/io/pickle.py#L95

read_pickle does not accept google storage URL (in form "gs://bucket-name/path/file.pkl") as input

While this code works fine:
`
with tf.io.gfile.GFile("gs://bucket-name/path/file.pkl", "rb") as infile:
      df = pd.read_pickle(infile, compression=None)
`

Might be reasonable to amend the documentation with this if the above is true for the recent version of pandas.
comments: Makes sense - should be in line with other IO functions I think
this is very easy to patch to actually read from uri

review_comments: Is the S3 or GCS restriction still accurate? You seem to have tests for general `http://` URLs.

I made `read_pickle` accept general URLs just because [`get_filepath_or_buffer` can send GET request to the URL using `urllib.request.urlopen()` (but only GET request)](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/master/pandas/io/common.py#L171-L179).
My test only checks `read_pickle` for now.

I can update `to_pikle` so that it'll send a POST request, please advise if it's better.
Understood. We can handle that elsewhere.
can you add a versionchanged tag here (1.0), noting the URLs

Added versionchanged tag for ver 1.0.0 to mention it accepts URLs

> ... versionchanged:: 1.0.0
> Accept URL. URL has to be of S3 or GCS.
is this necessary? get_handle i believe does this already

I think it is.
[`get_handle` calls `infer_compression` only when `path_or_buffer` is a string](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/master/pandas/io/common.py#L388-L389).
So if we hand over a buffer, `compression` stays as "infer", and later on, [it'll raise ValueError if the compression is not "gzip", "bz2", "zip", nor "xz".](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/master/pandas/io/common.py#L391-L433)

Please advise what's the best here, thank you!
